MEMO (reps-vs-diligence-memo.docx) | Privileged | To: C. Reeves; cc T. Avery | PrecisionFlow reps vs diligence | Mar. 2025

BOTTOM LINE
Do not sign on the Seller draft. Critical items: (1) Kessler COC termination and Monterrey landlord consent, absent from Schedules (about $68M revenue); (2) Karen Beecham title claim; (3) Dayton ownership contradicted by the contract summary; (4) Schedules do not track the SPA (numbering, 5,000,000 vs 1,000,000 shares, a patent list matching none of the IP memo's 14, six ABL lender names). Fix known breaches by price, specific indemnity or closing condition: Art. VIII and Sec. 2.5 are not in the excerpt (cap, basket, survival unverified) and SPA 4.7 recites Buyer's investigation. Delaware is pro-sandbagging absent contrary text (Arwood v. AW Site Servs., Del. Ch. Mar. 9, 2022, actual-knowledge test) but governing law is unseen; add an express clause. Unreconciled source conflicts are marked UNRESOLVED.

SEVERITY KEY: C=Critical (price/closing/title); H=High; M=Medium; L=Low.

A. DISCREPANCY MAP

1. Kessler COC termination (C). SPA 3.15(a)(iv) requires listing COC/termination-right contracts; Schedule 3.15 lists Kessler ($29.4M, 20.6%) without Sec. 12.3 (60-day termination on >50% change); 3.2(c)(iii) no-conflict rep also false. Source: contract summary CC-001; diligence report VIII.B. Action: pre-signing waiver or closing condition; revenue-retention escrow/earn-out; correct Schedules 3.15/3.4. The IP memo says PF-4200 is sold to Kessler, compounding AquaDyne risk.

2. Monterrey lease consent (C). Lease needs landlord consent to indirect COC (summary: Sec. 8.4, 60 days' PRIOR notice, default then 30-day termination; diligence report cites Sec. 14.2: section conflict, UNRESOLVED). Not on Schedule 3.4/5.3, which says "no other consents." Monterrey = $38.2M (26.7%) revenue. 60-day notice means notice by about May 1 for a June 30 closing. Action: add to 5.3, closing condition, serve notice now.

3. Karen Beecham claim (C). SPA 3.3(d) (title free of Encumbrances; "Encumbrance" includes "claim"); Schedule 3.2 says Hal's shares free and clear. Diligence: 2021 decree gives Karen 5% of Hal's shares (3.1% of company); Hal disputes; post-decree proceedings pending (Denton, oral, Feb. 20); no order produced. Hal's January 2025 board presentation was silent. Value about $8.9M at $287M (about $8M at equity value net of $34.2M debt). Hal is also Seller Representative and signs the Schedules. Action: decree, settlement, docket; release or court order as closing condition; escrow of about $8.9M; schedule it; Karen joinder if she holds an interest; candor flag to R. Mehta; consider delaying signing.

4. Dayton owned vs leased (C, UNRESOLVED). SPA 3.7(a), Schedule 3.18 and the diligence title search: owned in fee, ABL mortgage. Contract summary OC-010: leased from Clearwater, $1.44M/yr to 12/2027. Also size: SPA 145,000 sf vs Schedules/report 185,000. Monterrey: SPA 62,000 sf vs 15,000 sf (Schedule, report) while generating $38.2M. Action: title commitment/deed, Clearwater lease; correct 3.7, Phase I and mortgage assumptions.

5. Schedules do not map to SPA (C/H). Schedule numbers are offset (e.g., Sched. 3.8 litigation vs SPA 3.10; 3.10 tax vs 3.14; 3.14 compliance vs 3.11; 3.18 real property vs 3.7). Missing: Schedules 3.11, 3.18 (brokers; workpaper shows $4.1M Seller banker/advisor costs), 3.19, 3.20, 2.5. Under the preamble, cross-disclosure applies only if "reasonably apparent on its face", so mislabelled items may fail to qualify, or may qualify the wrong rep.

6. Capitalization (H). SPA 3.3(a): 1,000,000 shares, $0.01 par; Schedule 3.2: 5,000,000 shares, $0.001 par (percentages agree). Pool holders (e.g., D. Caldwell "CFO", K. Lindquist "GC") conflict with Peretti (CFO) and Cho (GC per report/email; "VP Operations" in the SPA Knowledge definition). SPA 3.3(c) says no rights; Schedule says RSAs accelerate on COC. Action: charter, ledger, Exhibit A; fix Knowledge group.

7. Investors' Rights Agreement (H). Schedule 3.15F/3.4: IRA (6/30/2016; tag/drag, information, observer rights; Sec. 4.2). SPA 3.3(e) says no shareholder agreements other than RSAs; neither the diligence report nor the contract summary reviews it. Action: obtain, terminate or waive at closing; correct 3.3(e).

8. Debt documents (H). ABL lender is named six ways: Heartland (SPA), Meridian National (Schedules), First Midwestern (report), Keystone National (IP memo), Midwestern Commercial (workpaper), Dayton Industrial (summary); term lender Heartland/Great River/others. Terms conflict: ABL maturity 5/15/2025 (Schedule) vs 6/30/2028 (summary); seller note 6.5% from 6/30/2016 maturing 6/30/2026 (SPA/Schedule) vs 8% PIK from 1/15/2018 maturing 1/14/2028 (summary), with mandatory prepayment on COC and accrued PIK above $3.0M. Action: credit agreements, UCC/lien search, payoff letters; guaranty ($1.8M) release; PIK-adjusted payoff in Indebtedness.

9. Adjusted EBITDA / COVID add-back (C, price). SPA 3.4(e) represents all four adjustments are non-recurring. Charges: FY22 $0.55M, FY23 $0.45M, FY24 $0.60M. Ridgeline's 3/6 breakdown: $0.38M recurring (expedited freight, premium pricing) and $0.22M defensible inventory write-down. Eliminating all $0.60M cuts price $5.7M ($281.3M); removing $0.38M cuts about $3.6M ($283.4M). The 3/10 report ignores the 3/6 split. SPA says comp add-back covers Beecham and Peretti; workpaper and email say Beecham only. Action: negotiate $0.22M ceiling or zero; delete the "each adjustment appropriate" rep or backstop it with a price-based indemnity; tighten Adjusted EBITDA definition.

10. EBITDA arithmetic (H, UNRESOLVED). Workpaper: gross profit $48.91M less opex "excl. D&A" $17.60M = $31.31M, but "EBITDA" shown is $26.41M, which equals the figure after deducting D&A $4.90M (FY22/FY23 same pattern). Either opex is mislabelled or reported "EBITDA" is EBIT. A $4.9M gap at 9.5x is about $46.6M of value, in either direction. Action: Ridgeline to reconcile to audited statements before pricing.

11. Net working capital (H). Dec. 31 NWC $29.8M vs Seller peg $18.4M = $11.4M surplus paid to Seller; peg unverified. The workpaper's quarter-end NWC ($16.9/20.3/25.1/29.8M) averages $23.0M, above $18.4M. Inventory up 21.6% vs revenue 8.7% may inflate NWC. Closing is measured June 30 (Q2 2024: $20.3M), so true exposure is smaller, but the peg looks low. Section 2.5 not provided. Action: monthly build, line-item consistency, inventory reserve review, reset peg or add collar.

12. Pension (H). SPA 3.16(e) and Schedule: $4.3M unfunded (Jan. 2024 valuation); Buyer's actuary $6.8M (+$2.5M; discount rate 5.4% to 4.6%). The rep recites a dated figure so it is technically accurate, but price and the "no Title IV liability other than as reflected" language mislead. Actuary named Millbrook (SPA), Cornerstone (Schedule) and Clarkfield (workpaper): reconcile (Clarkfield is also auditor). Action: treat unfunded pension as debt-like at updated figure; bring-down valuation within 60 days of closing; specific indemnity.

13. California tax (C). SPA 3.14(a) (all returns filed), 3.14(i) (nexus only OH/MI/IN/IL/TX/DE) and Schedule 3.10(4) are inaccurate: San Jose rep since 1/2022; about $3.8M CA sales FY24; no CA returns. Diligence range $100-300K tax plus 25% penalty, interest, $800/yr minimum. My cross-check: 3.8/143 = 2.7% apportionment x roughly $22-26M pre-tax x 8.84% = about $50-60K/yr, consistent. Caveats: no filing means the assessment period generally stays open (verify R&TC 19057), so exposure may predate 2022; also CA sales/use tax collection, EDD payroll and foreign qualification (3.1(d)) are unquantified. Possible P.L. 86-272 defense (solicitation-only; in-home office allowed), but the $800 minimum tax is unprotected and the facts are unknown. Action: CA tax counsel; voluntary disclosure before FTB contact; confirm no FTB notices; specific tax indemnity outside basket/cap with dedicated escrow; correct 3.14 and Schedule.

14. NOLs / Sec. 382 (M). SPA 3.14(f) and Schedule disclose 382 limitation generally; SPA has no no-prior-ownership-change rep. Ridgeline's concern is Cascadia's CFO modelling full use. My estimate (unverified rate): annual limit is equity value (about $250M) x long-term tax-exempt rate (about 3-4%), which is roughly $8-10M and above $4.1M, so the limit may not bind, though Sec. 172 80% cap applies. Red flag: with $26M EBITDA since 2021, why is a FY2020 NOL still $4.1M? Possibly original, not remaining. Action: NOL roll-forward by year; add rep: no prior ownership change, remaining balance, no 382/383 limits; tax group to confirm computation.

15. R&D credits / transfer pricing (M). IRS exam of FY21-22 credits ($1.3M of $2.7M) is disclosed, but 3.14(e) "reasonable basis" for all $2.7M remains exposed. Transfer pricing: SPA 3.14(h) says Company to Subsidiary at cost-plus 8%; Schedule says Monterrey to Dayton. The report's "properly disclosed" is therefore doubtful. Action: TP study; specific indemnity.

16. IP schedule (H/C). Schedule 3.9 lists 12 patents; the report and IP memo say 14 and 2 omitted (10,891,234; 10,891,235, both PF-4200). But none of the 12 scheduled patent numbers or titles matches the 12 others in the IP memo's table, and the 3 pending applications and trademark list also differ (Schedule has second mark 4,012,567). The "two omitted" framing therefore understates a wholesale mismatch; USPTO assignment search is mandatory. SPA 3.9(b) validity/enforceability is unqualified.

17. AquaDyne (C). SPA 3.9(c) and Schedule 3.8 recite the Hargrove & Lind opinion and "without merit" without its limitation. Scope conflict: report says claim 14 only (1-13 and 15-22 covered); IP memo says 14-22 disclaimed: UNRESOLVED; read the opinion. Testing data withheld three times (1/28, 2/11, 2/25). PF-4200 is about $22M (15%) of revenue. IP memo's willfulness point is overstated: failure to obtain counsel advice cannot prove willfulness (35 U.S.C. 298); the data refusal and knowledge after the 9/8/2024 letter are the real risk. Action: data, supplemental opinion as closing condition, special IP indemnity/escrow, add 3.21 disclosure.

18. Environmental (C/H). SPA 3.12 and Schedule 3.12 disclose only the 2023 spill. The Oct. 2024 Greenleaf Phase I found a REC (chlorinated solvents, NE corner, pre-2004 tenant) and recommends Phase II; not scheduled; 3.12(c) (all reports delivered) and (a)(iii) knowledge rep are doubtful. Current-owner CERCLA liability follows the Company in a stock deal (no BFPP protection for the Company's own liability). Action: Phase II pre-closing, correct Schedule, environmental indemnity/escrow, PLL policy. Ownership question (item 4) affects who bears liability.

19. Martinez / insurance (H). SPA 3.10(c) and 3.13(d): litigation "adequately covered." CGL $10M per occurrence vs $12M demand plus punitive; ROR reserves punitive exclusion. Conflict: SPA 3.13(b)(v) lists $15M Continental umbrella; Schedule 3.13 says "None"; report omits it: UNRESOLVED; if the umbrella exists the gap may close. Policy numbers conflict. Summary says CGL expired 12/31/2024, renewal pending, vs through 12/31/2025; COC requires insurer notice within 30 days. Workers' comp and other coverages are misaligned. Action: policies, defence counsel assessment, carve-out of Martinez from 3.10(c), specific indemnity; tail/renewal confirmation.

20. Material contracts list (H). Schedule 3.15 omits Summit Valve ($5.8M), Bridger Creek ($4.7M, $3M minimum), Hawkins ($6.8M spend) and Clearwater, though the summary says "properly disclosed"; and omits Overland MFN (3.15(a)(ii)) and the Dunlap $10M minimum. Dunlap, Great Plains and Overland dates conflict across Schedule, summary and workpaper (Dunlap expiry 5/31/2025 vs 5/31/2026 vs 8/31/2025); top-10 customer names differ. NorthPoint ($18.6M, 13%) expired 2/28/2025: "in full force" (3.15(c)) false; either party can end on 90 days' notice under 9.1 anyway. Action: obtain all contracts, renewal as condition, conform list; confirm Great Plains/Dunlap renewal windows fall before closing.

21. Verteon (M, UNRESOLVED). Schedule and IP memo: non-transferable, consent possibly needed; summary Sec. 12.1 and report: license survives COC. Read Sec. 12.1 or seek consent (SPA 3.9(f)).

22. OSHA (M). SPA 3.11(c) says all citations fully resolved and Schedule 3.11 lists two; Oct. 2024 serious lockout/tagout citation ($28,700) is contested (Schedules 3.6/3.14 disclose it under wrong numbers). Rep 3.11(a) three-year compliance affected. Action: add to 3.11; lockout/tagout program review; accrual.

23. Headcount (M, UNRESOLVED). SPA 3.17: 730 (485+170+75). Schedule: Dayton 485 already includes 75 corporate, so its table sums to 655. Report: 740 (485+180+75). Payroll census needed. Non-competes: Schedule 2 years vs IP memo 18 months. CIC exposure $3.01M is arithmetically right and double-trigger.

24. Other (L). Diligence obtained only DE/OH good-standing certificates; SPA 3.1(d) claims MI/IN/IL/TX too: obtain. Verified consistent: revenue ($118.2M/$131.6M/$143.0M), CIC math, escrow $22.96M (8%), debt $34.2M, top-5 58%.

B. PRIORITY ACTIONS BEFORE MARCH 14
(1) Request: decree/docket, Kessler waiver, landlord notice, deed and Clearwater lease, credit agreements, AquaDyne opinion/data, Phase II, charter/ledger, IRA, NOL roll-forward, umbrella policy.
(2) Conformed Schedules before signing.
(3) Markup: specific indemnities (California tax, Karen, AquaDyne, environmental, pension, Martinez); closing conditions (Kessler, NorthPoint, landlord, Karen release); pro-sandbagging; no schedule-update cure; 382 rep; correct Knowledge group.
(4) Price: COVID add-back ($3.6-5.7M), EBITDA reconciliation, NWC peg, pension to debt.
(5) Advise Kowalski on NOLs; brief Mehta on Seller disclosure pattern; consider delaying signing if Karen, Dayton or lender conflicts persist.
